_what: Trainer-shape throughput microbenchmark on the RTX 3080, run 2026-09-04 during the M10 plan review to test the plan's imported planning rate (560 examples/s, LEAF's realized A100 rate). RANDOM TOKEN IDS ONLY: no corpus text, no protected path, no teacher, no data loading, no evaluation. It bounds the HARDWARE, not the pipeline; the real-data re-measure (m10/STATUS.md box-window item 1) is what the build's cost line reads.
model: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 + Linear(1152->1024) applied per token over concat of hidden layers 12/8/4, then masked mean pool + L2 normalize

pass1_2026-09-04.note: first pass; superseded by pass 2 for every shape it repeats. Kept because the two-chunk row and the plain-vs-fused AdamW comparison are only here.

bs32_mix7525_two_chunks_adamw.note: M9's collate: query and document chunks stepped separately inside one optimizer step

bs32_mix7525_two_chunks_fused_adamw.note: fused AdamW makes no difference; the cost is not the optimizer

bs512_mix7525_fused.note: SUPERSEDED READING: pass 1 called this 'past the launch-bound regime'. Pass 2 shows 512x64 and 128x256 each reach 185-191K padded tok/s at 7.0 GB peak, so this two-chunk 57K-token step was memory-bound on a 10 GB card, not evidence about the compute regime. Flagged by the Fable review.

pass2_2026-09-04.note: single homogeneous chunk per step (what length bucketing produces), 300 timed steps, peak memory and allocator retries logged. This is the pass to cite.

bs32_doc_bucket_256.note: the shape 25% of build steps will run under length bucketing; untimed in pass 1, added on the Fable review

reading: Launch-bound at batch 32 is now established rather than asserted: 4x the tokens per step (32x64 -> 32x256) costs only 20% more wall-clock, and 4x the batch at fixed length (32x64 -> 128x64) costs 24%. The card's throughput roof is 185-191K padded tokens/s, reached only at 128x256 and 512x64; batch 32 runs at 24-80% of it. Allocator retries were 0 in every pass-2 row, so pass 1's slow bs512 two-chunk row was memory pressure on 10 GB, not a compute-regime change.

build_cost_under_length_bucketing.method: 200M examples at the mandate's 75/25 example mix = 150M query-bucket examples + 50M document-bucket examples, each at its own measured rate
build_cost_under_length_bucketing.bs128_is_cheaper_by: 2.2x, which family E must weigh against any bs32 quality win

the_caveat_that_binds: These are hardware bounds. M9's realized pipeline ran at 18,984 tok/s (m9/M92_LOCK.md) against a comparable-shape hardware roof of ~191K here, i.e. roughly 10% efficiency, and the M10 trainer is being ported from that pipeline (m9src/longrun.py: per-step numpy collate, length_chunks, target fetch). Until the real-data re-measure lands, the build must be priced as a RANGE from hardware bound to M9 efficiency, and no dollar or box-vs-cloud decision may rest on the optimistic end alone. Raised by the Fable review of 2026-09-04.
